thinking: We are asked to review the original verdict and consider the panel's reasoning. The original verdict as Bill Ackman was bearish with 85% confidence, citing no margin of safety, no catalyst, and overvaluation. Now we see all other experts' verdicts. Many are bearish (Buffett, Burry, Damodaran, Druckenmiller, Graham, Pabrai, Taleb) with varying confidence, some neutral (Jhunjhunwala, Lynch, Munger, Wood), and few bullish (Bullish Advocate 65%, Fisher 78%). The Ackman perspective focuses on activism potential, catalyst, and margin of safety. The key data: price 2435, DCF 1868 (30% overvalued), PEG 1.99, ROE 32.58%, growth 71.6% YoY, institutional selling heavy, technical breakdown. No clear activist catalyst to unlock value. The bullish arguments rely on forward estimates (EPS 93 implying forward PE 26.2) and strong growth, but as Ackman, I need a clear undervaluation (>30% upside) and a fixable catalyst. The DCF suggests downside, not upside. The activism potential is nil: no underperforming segments to spin off, no poor capital allocation to correct. So even revising, the verdict remains bearish. Confidence might adjust based on other experts' reasoning but still high. I might consider whether the sell-off itself creates an activist opportunity (buyback? restructure?) but the company is already performing well, so no. Thus, I will maintain bearish, confidence maybe 80 or 85. The original 85 seems fine. No need to change. I'll output the reasoning with specific numbers.
